analysis: Only .github/scripts/test-threat-bedrock.py changed: it is an offline CI test file for the threat-review tooling and does not touch provider code, the coordinator WebSocket contract, App Attest, keys, or any runtime path in the canonical threat model (TB-002, TB-011, A-015/A-016). It adds tests for a 'workload' Bedrock call policy: stage admission through plan_calls, an emergency ceiling raising BEDROCK_WORKLOAD_LIMIT, rejection of invalid policy and ceiling values (>100, 0, unknown policy), an end-to-end large-scan test with real segmentation, and tests that incomplete final results always require a human and are never marked clean. The tests use synthetic clients and do not spend money; they assert fallback.calls == [] and clean()==False for errors, uncovered units, a missing integration, pending depth batches and limited files. No weakening of existing gate or merge-policy assertions is visible in this diff. The implementation of the new behavior (threat_review.bedrock, budget_scan, budget_runner, merge_policy) is not in the supplied units, so correctness of the workload policy, cost bounding and clearance logic cannot be verified here. The tests assert fail-closed behavior, but the implementation should be checked in the files in the other batches. No threat-model change is warranted from this file alone.
